- Oyu Tolgoi. Mining.com's "begins restarting" headline lands a day after we logged the seismic pause with no duration. If restart is real and quick, it undercuts the margin-story worry I raised on 30 October. But "begins" is not "resumed," and there is no output figure. The 70% export drop from China's border checks is a separate question. Nothing here shows the two touch the same tonnes, so Dr I Simon is right to keep them apart. Yukon's concentrate-import channel stays open.

- Gold. "Gold price slumps to one-year low, silver breaks $50" is the first sharp price move on the desk's radar, but it is a headline with no dated series. It also sits awkwardly with the record. Crux's "above US$4,000" claim is unsourced, and Yahoo reported gold below $4,100 on 28 October. If gold is near $4,000, Harmony's price deck matters more, and it is due in today's 6-K filing. We still don't have it. Separately, the Eldorado Q3 call summary suggests quarterly results may already be out. If so, our 15 November Eldorado prediction could be moot or wrongly timed. Check the release date before scoring it.

- Codelco. An accounting scandal now touching eight more employees is governance, not tonnes. It does matter for Andes Norte, though. A company under internal scrutiny may be slower to publish restart detail, and that cuts against our restart predictions.

- Copper. Nothing here moves the copper view. Highland Valley's strike remains unsized. Capstone's "double production" framing needs a base year before it means anything. The 16 October LME settlement is still unlogged, so the 30 October checkpoint stays blocked.

Colleague note, Fri 30 October, midday. Most of today's headlines are commentary or background, so I've focused on the five that touch the record.

- Oyu Tolgoi is restarting. Mining.com's headline says Rio Tinto has "begun restarting" the underground after the seismic pause. That means a start, not a resumption, and it comes from a headline with no company release behind it. It still matters for my channel. The pause only becomes a multi-quarter margin story if it runs long, and a restart under way lowers that odds. It doesn't touch the China border story. Dr I Simon is right that the record still doesn't show the 70% export drop and the pause involving the same tonnes. Until Rio quantifies, the two stay separate.

- Copper is still unscored. The 16 October LME settlement remains unlogged, so the 30 October checkpoint stays blocked. Nothing in this batch fixes that.

- Highland Valley and Capstone. The CIM roundup pairs the Teck strike with Capstone's plan to "double" Chilean copper. The record has Capstone's US$3bn with no capex split or base year, so "double" has no base yet. The Teck strike still has no stated duration or tonnage. Teck's Q3 results, due by 15 November, are the first place either gets a number, and the same filing should give the period and earnings figure behind the "profit surge" headline.

- Gold. MINING.COM says gold hit a one-year low with silver above $50. There is no price series, date or source. Crux's "above US$4,000" claim is still unsourced, and Yahoo put gold below $4,100 earlier. The $4,000 level is the number everyone is talking about, so I'd rather test it than argue about it.

- Codelco. The accounting scandal story, with eight more employees named, is governance news. Nothing in the record links it to the Andes Norte halt or the blockade, and I won't draw that line.

Elsewhere: Yahoo's Eldorado call recap suggests the Q3 release may already be out. Check the release itself for restated guidance and the Skouries figure, since a call summary is secondhand. Perseus's backup power at Nyanzaga is part of the same power theme, but there is no grid attribution yet. The rest (Curzio, ETF Database, the Phys.org copper history, Veramark, the CAMIMEX targets) is commentary or background.

chief_sessions.opening:
Initial read

The most solid conclusions are the ones that refuse to score what the record can't support. Copper stays unscored because the 16 October LME settlement is still unlogged, and that blocks the 30 October checkpoint. Oyu Tolgoi is held as a timing question, not a confirmed supply loss, and "restarting" is correctly kept apart from "resumed." The 70% export drop and the pause are still unlinked by any tonnage, so they should stay separate. Dropping the LBMA sub-$4,000 prediction was right, because no verified gold print anchors it.

The thinnest reasoning is in the precious-metals predictions. The silver item asks for a close below $50, but the record only shows silver "breaking" $50 in a headline with no series, and no named benchmark is attached. That doesn't support medium confidence. The gold items are better, but they still hang on an unsourced price level. Yukon's named-benchmark wording is the right fix, and it should be applied to silver too.

Two items need checking before anything else is scored. The Eldorado Q3 release may already be out, which would make the 15 November predictions moot or mistimed. The Teck Q3 date also decides whether the strike predictions can resolve at all. Both are release-date checks, not analysis.

QUESTIONS FOR THE STRATEGIST:
- For silver and gold, which single named daily benchmark will the desk use, and does the same series govern every price-threshold prediction? If the silver item stays at medium confidence, what evidence raises it above the headline?
- If Rio confirms an Oyu Tolgoi restart but gives no volumes, what base rate would you apply to judge whether the pause becomes a multi-quarter margin story? Which signpost would make you drop the margin thesis?
- Gold and silver are both moving on flows. Does a sustained precious-metals fall change any of the desk's supply-side or cost calls, such as Centerra, Eldorado or the broader cost-curve view, or is it only a sentiment test?

QUESTIONS FOR THE GEOLOGIST:
- Can you confirm from the primary source whether Eldorado's Q3 2026 release is already out? If it is, does it restate 2026 guidance and quantify the Skouries effect, and what happens to the 15 November predictions?
- For a staged underground restart after a seismic event, which wording in a Rio release would show which levels are back in production, and what is a typical re-entry and ground-support sign-off period, labelled as background?
- When is Teck's Q3 2026 release due, and does its planned wording state the Highland Valley strike's end date or affected copper tonnes? If the date falls outside the window, which prediction should be retired?
chief_sessions.strategist_answer:
On benchmarks: I'd use one named daily series for every precious-metals threshold, the LBMA Gold Price PM for gold and the LBMA Silver Price for silver. Both are published by a named administrator (background knowledge; the desk should confirm current publication details before scoring). Yukon was right about the benchmark. My objection was to the anchor, because we have no verified print behind the sub-$4,000 level. The same logic applies to silver. The "through US$50" headline has no series or date, so my medium confidence was too high. I'm downgrading it and restating it against the named benchmark:

On Oyu Tolgoi, I don't have a sourced base rate, so I won't invent one. Historically, staged restarts after ground-control pauses tend to take weeks to months before they show in output (background, not a figure from this batch). The margin thesis needs a Rio signpost: a stated underground throughput, or a guidance or cost revision in its quarterly review. If Rio confirms restart, reports ore flowing, and keeps guidance intact, I'd drop the multi-quarter margin story. A guidance cut would strengthen it.

On whether precious-metals weakness changes supply calls: for now it's a sentiment test. It would change my cost-curve view only if it shows up in company actions such as deferred drilling, a mothballed mill, or capex cuts. I don't have all-in sustaining cost figures for Centerra or Eldorado in this material, so I can't say whether either is near its cost floor. Until those numbers are sourced, I'd leave the supply calls unchanged and watch for those actions.
chief_sessions.geologist_answer:
On Eldorado, I can't confirm from the record whether the Q3 2026 release is out. The desk has only a note that it "may already be out." Before anyone scores the 15 November predictions, someone needs to check the company's news page or SEDAR+ directly. If the release is out, the 15 November predictions are moot, and the first things to check are whether 2026 guidance was restated and whether the Skouries effect was quantified in tonnes or dollars, not just described.

On Oyu Tolgoi, background only: a staged underground restart after a seismic event usually means inspection, scaling and ground-support checks, then re-entry level by level, and only then ore flowing to surface. In my experience that can take days to several weeks, and longer if damage is found. The wording that would actually show production is back is specific, not "restarting" or "resumed." I'd look for named levels or zones returned to production, a geotechnical or ground-support sign-off, first ore hoisted or delivered to the mill from underground, and a tonnage figure for the period. "Operations have begun restarting" tells you very little.

I should also correct my own prediction. My Oyu Tolgoi item asks for confirmation that underground operations "have resumed." That is a harder bar than "restarting," and it may not be met by 30 November even if work is going well. I'd treat a "restarting" release as partial evidence, not a resolution.

On Teck, I don't have the Q3 2026 release date in the material, so I can't say whether it falls before 15 November. My low-confidence prediction assumed it would, and it may not. If Teck reports after 15 November, retire that prediction now rather than leaving it open. The strike's end date or tonnes affected may still appear in the release, but the timing window is what decides whether it can resolve.
chief_sessions.conclusion:
BIG TAKEAWAYS:
